violated_contract: A one-time persisted-default migration must classify the install cohort using state that is stable across launches. Deciding 'existing vs fresh install' from a flag the same install flips during its first launch (onboarding completion) makes every later launch re-run the classification after the flip and pin fresh installs to the existing-user default, silently inverting the rollout default the feature shipped with.
canonical_prevention: Decide the cohort on the first launch that runs the migration build and write an explicit cohort marker in the same pass (marker write ordered so a crash re-runs the decision instead of half-applying it). Later launches consult only the marker, never re-derive cohort from mutable lifecycle flags. Behavioral contract test simulates launch-1 and launch-2 against both cohorts.
